rule: each point must stay inside its box on every commanded substep, else the chunk is refused and the run stops. Wall boxes keep 70 mm (30 margin + 40 for jaws, cables and link width); the tcp keeps 20 mm above the floor bound so a vertical gripper's fingertips (about 34 mm past the tcp) press at most about 8 mm; the hand stays 120 mm in front of J1.
z_shift_2026_11_08: Gavin raised the arm's base: every z lower bound moved down 25 mm with the floor and every upper bound down 16 mm with the rim, so each point keeps the clearance to the glass it was designed with. The first live Dream call (runs/live-20261108T205544Z) asked for tcp z = 16 mm, ~47 mm above the real floor, and the old box refused it.
near_shift_2026_11_08: Back wall moved from the 40 mm estimate to Gavin's 80 mm: elbow x max -30 -> +10 and wrist_pitch -20 -> +20 (same 70 / 60 mm from the wall as designed; the tank guard still checks every mesh vertex). The elbow limit cut 13 of 17 calls in live 20261108T212338Z while Dream's hand was 32-39 cm out.
floor_lowered_2026_11_08: Gavin: decrease the floor limit by 3 cm. tcp and wrist z min -5 -> -35, so the grasp centre can reach a golf ball's centre on the floor (~-10). The tank guard is then the binding floor limit: every mesh vertex at most 10 mm below the -31 mm floor line (gentle press, ~5 N at the hand with the 90/4 gains).
mount_shift_2026_11_13: New base mount (CAD from Gavin's 3MF, 2026-11-13): the back plane is the truss post's face 106 mm behind J1 (was 80), and with the post centred on Gavin's marker lines the side walls are +227 / -207 (were 210 / -224). Only the limits that were derived from a wall moved, each by the wall's own shift so it keeps its designed distance: elbow x max +10 -> +36 and wrist_pitch +20 -> +46 (+26, still 70 / 60 mm from the plane), and every point's y range [-154, 140] -> [-137, 157] (+17, still 70 mm from each side wall; the -y limit tightens because that wall is now closer). tcp (-120) and wrist (-60) x maxima are J1-relative and stay. The x minima (-624, -600) still come from the old -694 far estimate and now sit past the far glass (-616): on the far side the tank guard (every mesh vertex, 70 mm) is the only wall check. The base can still slide or rotate under a push on the glass; neither the box nor the guard can see that.
